scope: Identity evidence for a compact third batch of members of the 2017 PCA Ad Interim Committee on Women Serving in the Ministry of the Church.
modeling_rule: These records support person-identity reconciliation only. They do not assign any report-level theological position, either internal school of thought, or broader ideological label to an individual committee member. Person-specific theological evidence must be normalized separately.

evidence.fact: The official 2017 General Assembly directory lists TE Jeffrey Choi of Metropolitan New York as a voting member of the Women Serving in the Ministry of the Church study committee.
The official 2019 General Assembly directory lists Jeffrey Choi as a Teaching Elder at Astoria Community in Metropolitan New York Presbytery.
Astoria Community Church reports that Jeffrey Choi attended the 2018 PCA General Assembly and served on the Committee for the Review of Presbytery Records.

A 2017 article authored by Jeffrey Choi describes his work on the women-in-ministry study committee and explains his dissent from one part of the report. The article is used here only as corroborating identity evidence; its theological content should be normalized separately if needed.

records.match_basis: The official 2017 committee directory identifies TE Jeffrey Choi with Metropolitan New York Presbytery; later official PCA records and Astoria Community Church independently place Jeffrey Choi in the same PCA presbytery/church context, while his first-person 2017 article explicitly identifies his committee participation.
records.reasoning_boundary: Identity only; Jeffrey Choi's separately attributable dissent and theological arguments are not converted into position data in this identity slice.

evidence.fact: The official 2017 committee roster prints Mrs. Kathy Keller as a Voting Member.
A contemporaneous New Life Presbyterian Church report on the 45th General Assembly identifies committee member Kathy Keller as Tim Keller's wife.
Redeemer Presbyterian Church publishes a first-person historical article under Kathy Keller in which she describes founding Redeemer with Tim Keller.
The PCA Bookstore identifies author Kathy Keller as co-founder of Redeemer Presbyterian Church and wife of Tim Keller.

records.match_basis: A contemporaneous PCA congregation explicitly identifies the committee's Kathy Keller as Tim Keller's wife, and Redeemer/PCA first-party biographical material independently identifies that Kathy Keller and her Redeemer role.
records.reasoning_boundary: Identity only; Kathy Keller's published views, Redeemer ministry practices, or relationship to Tim Keller are not converted into broader ideological labels or committee-position attribution in this slice.
